## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
After the recent overhaul of the kodi integration, the media player entity is `unavailable` when Home Assistant starts until the related kodi instance comes online. This prevents the power button from showing up on the media player card.
This PR changes the behavior so the media player entities are `off` at startup, allowing for power-on actions through the UI.
The changes are largely based on changes made by https://github.com/alexanv1/core/commit/571780f5048879bfe9a19ff9e29fca5dd42037e5 with some additional fixes as mentioned in the discussion of the issue at #40450

issue_context.title: Kodi entity is "off" for long time after kodi is back online
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
The kodi entity stays "off" for a long time after kodi is back online and reachable.
It also does not submit commands to kodi during that time.

Use case:
To save energy my kodi-pc is always suspended.
Whenever I want to play music or a video, it should come out of sleep and start playing instantly.
I do this with a script that sends a WOL, waits 3 seconds, and initiates playback.

But... The kodi entity stays "off" sometimes for minutes after kodi is back online.
Home assistant even refuses to send any kodi.call_method during that period.
It probably has to do with other issues that I've seen on similar topics, indicating the problems with the watchdog that only checks if kodi is online every 3 minutes.

The request in this issue report is to implement a solution, any of these would be a good step:

1. Make every call to kodi (e.g. kodi.call_method) secretly "under water" behave as follows:
Check state of kodi entity. 
If on/idle/playing/etc, send the kodi call. 
If off, perform turn_on action (which can be user defined already), wait for user-defined timeout (set in integration configuration), then execute the actual kodi call.

2. On every call to kodi, "secretly under water" perform a poll if kodi is "off", as follows:
Check state of kodi entity.
if on/idle/playing/etc, send the kodi call.
if off, poll once.
If poll indicates kodi is online, set kodi entity state to online, and execute the actual kodi call.

3. Instant detection of kodi coming back online.
Either via polling, detecting kodi uPnP event on network (Kodi's SSDP service discovery broadcast message perhaps?), detecting a dhcpdiscover packet from the kodi PC and poll more frequently after that; anything that could work.
Downside of this method is that where-ever the user implements a call to kodi in a script/automation/etc, an explicit check needs to be added first by the user.

4. As alternative, implement a "force check now" method that can be executed via a script
4b. This would also enable the kodi-pc to execute a rpc json call on home assistant as soon as it is back online, removing the need for repeated polling. The kodi-pc can then connect to home assistant and tell it's back online.
4c. This would also enable the user to create an intervalled shell_command that pings or ssh's to the kodi pc (or wget to 8080) to check it's status, and when it's online, forces the kodi-poll.
Not pretty, but at least then we have options.

5. As alternative, implement a settable watchdog timer that can be customized with YAML and/or via the UI

In the end; having to wait up to 3 minutes before the music starts playing is quite annoying. 

And waiting until kodi is up before executing the "actual" user's request  is not feasible; I have a lot of different scripts handling different user-requests to kodi. All of them would have to support the "wait until kodi is finally reachable", which creates a mess.



## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.117.2 
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 4.15
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): OS on Nuc
- Integration causing this issue: Kodi
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/kodi/

comments:
Likely fixed by https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/41714

I just did the review for it with suggested changes to move it forward

@bdraco ,good news then!
I have checked the issues on the solve list of that PR.
But I don't yet understand the fix completely.

The watchdog will go from 3 minutes to 10 seconds.

But still, imagine you want to do a call to kodi from a script, or a lovelace button.
Then everywhere we want that, and for every button, we will have to implement a "wait until kodi entity is online, then do the call" workaround in a script.. That is very impractical, and that does not seem to get solved here.

The best solution would be to make all calls to kodi "blocking", with a timeout, in which the integration tries to get kodi online first.
Only then will calling a "hey kodi, please play" to a kodi that is in suspend, actually work without much much scripting overhead.
